strategy_title: Autotune XBLOCK/R0_BLOCK Causes Register Spill Regression
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with larger XBLOCK and R0_BLOCK configs caused the compiler to allocate 255 registers per thread (up from 128), halving the block limit from 4 to 2 blocks/SM and dropping theoretical occupancy from 25% to 12.5%. This worsened scheduler eligibility (No Eligible rose from 40% to 56%) and increased kernel duration by ~42% despite waves/SM doubling from 0.97 to 1.94. The root cause is that autotuning configs with larger tile sizes (e.g. R0_BLOCK=4096, 8192) force the compiler to keep more live values in registers simultaneously, exhausting the register file and causing spills that dominate over any coalescing or wave-count benefit.
applicable_when: Never apply this specific pattern when the kernel already uses 128+ registers/thread and the register block limit is already the binding occupancy constraint (Block Limit Registers < Block Limit Warps). Autotune with large tile configs is only safe when register pressure is low (e.g. <64 regs/thread) and occupancy is not register-limited.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel already has registers_per_thread >= 128 and Block Limit Registers is the binding occupancy constraint. Adding autotune configs with R0_BLOCK > current value will push register count to 255 (hardware max), halving occupancy and worsening scheduler stall rates. Also avoid when the kernel has a Welford reduction accumulating multiple live tensors across a large R0_BLOCK loop body.
framework_notes: Triton's @triton.autotune selects configs at runtime but the compiler must compile all configs. Large R0_BLOCK values (4096, 8192) in a Welford reduction kernel with multiple live accumulators (mean, m2, weight) cause the register allocator to spill or max out at 255 regs/thread. In CUDA, the equivalent risk is __launch_bounds__ with large tile sizes in reduction kernels. Always check that the winning autotune config does not increase registers_per_thread beyond the baseline.
